items.content:
RT @aakashgupta: Cookie stuffing already sent two men to federal prison. Shawn Hogan made $28 million as eBay's #1 affiliate before the FBI raided his home. Brian Dunning, the #2, took in $5.2 million. Both pleaded guilty to wire fraud.

Now leaked Slack messages show Phoebe Gates' startup ran the same playbook, and the founders knew.

Here's what Phia's extension did. During checkout it opened a background tab and inserted its own referral code, claiming commission on sales it never drove, sometimes overriding the affiliate who actually earned it. Nike and Nordstrom were among the retailers hit.

When Bloomberg first reported it in July, Phia called it a bug and said the company had just learned of it. The new leaks show Gates and Kianni discussing the practice with engineers back in December. Seven months earlier. And per Bloomberg, the code was a deliberately built feature with a toggle.

Bugs don't ship with on/off switches.

The wildest thread runs through one man. In 2006, eBay hired a fraud researcher named Ben Edelman to run compliance checks on affiliates suspected of cookie stuffing, the cases that became the Hogan and Dunning prosecutions. In 2026, the researcher who reviewed Phia's code and concluded it was designed to claim unearned commissions? Ben Edelman. Same investigator, same scheme, 20 years apart.

The eBay cases are also why the 20-year max is real. Prosecutors argued the cookies themselves, transmitted across state lines, constituted the wire fraud. That theory won, and it turned cookie stuffing into a federal crime.

Hogan got 5 months. Dunning got 15. Both were first offenses.

items.content:
RT @Itsfoss: The man who built CentOS and Rocky Linux is now trying to do for AI what open source did for operating systems.

Gregory Kurtzer just launched OpenWALDO, a transparent AI training dataset containing 167 billion tokens sourced from government records, academic papers, mailing lists, and public domain literature.

- Every token is traceable
- Every source is documented
- Every license is accounted for
- No rare books harmed in the process

Kurtzer's pitch is simple: "Linux didn't win by being certified safe. It won by being inspectable, forkable, and community validated."

He thinks the same logic applies to AI.

A lab or company can take OpenWALDO's corpus, verify its sources, add their own proprietary data on top, and ship a model with a clean, auditable lineage.

That is something no one building on (unethically) scraped internet data can offer today.

The project is funded by CIQ, Kurtzer's company behind Rocky Linux, and is looking for contributors.

The open source world built the internet's infrastructure once before. There is no reason it cannot do it again, this time for AI.

I am rooting for OpenWALDO.

items.content:
My short debugging story...

NVIDIA: i'll initialize graphics during early boot.
ZFS: bro I'm still trying to exist.
Me: spends 3 hours becoming a ZFS administrator with panic attack 💀. 

TL;DR:- 

> Installed Nvidia driver
> reboots my workstation. 
> GRUB loads.
> and then... nothing.💀
> live booted.
> start digging through ZFS.
> trying to figure out which ZFS dataset was actually /.
> Chroot fails because /usr/bin/bash apparently doesn't exist. 💀
> At this point i was like: wait... is /usr its own ZFS dataset?
> Yep. Something had mounted that shit over the real /usr.
> Unmount it.
> Suddenly /usr/bin/bash magically exists.
> WTF ? 💀
> okay, i am inside the chroot system now.
> check NVIDIA.
> DKMS looks fine.
> disable NVIDIA modesetting.
> rebuild initramfs.
> and then: dracut: Invalid tmpdir '/var/tmp'
> panic attack for a sec. 💀
> create /var/tmp.
> rebuild again.
> Relief 😌
> Rebooted. i thought  it's over now...
> Looks into it.
> ZFS emergency shell. 
> Looked into it 
> no pools available
> no datasets available
> Aii YEEOOO 💀 

At this point I'm staring at the screen wondering how installing an NVIDIA driver somehow turned into a fucking ZFS archaeology expedition.

Look through the ZFS stuff went thru different forms for answers. 
> they told to import rpool, bpool and exit. 
> Done exactly 
> Everything works now = ) 

I just wanted to install GPU driver bro 😭

items.content:
RT @ptdbugs: A PoC/exploit has been discovered for vulnerability CVE-2026-68138

Vendor: Linux
Product: Linux
Description: In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

net/sched: serialize qdisc_rtab_list against concurrent get/put

qdisc_get_rtab() and qdisc_put_rtab() mutate the process-global singly
linked list qdisc_rtab_list and a plain non-atomic 'int refcnt' with no
lock. This was only safe because every caller historically held the RTNL
mutex, which serialized all rate-table lookups, inserts and frees.

That invariant no longer holds. cls_flower sets
TCF_PROTO_OPS_DOIT_UNLOCKED, so tc_new_tfilter() keeps rtnl_held == false
for it and sets TCA_ACT_FLAGS_NO_RTNL. That flag propagates through
tcf_exts_validate_ex() -> tcf_action_init() -> tcf_action_init_1() ->
tcf_police_init(), which calls qdisc_get_rtab()/qdisc_put_rtab() with the
RTNL mutex NOT held. Two RTM_NEWTFILTER requests on different CPUs, each
adding a flower filter with a police action carrying the same rate, then
race on qdisc_rtab_list and on the non-atomic refcnt, leading to a
use-after-free / double-free of the kmalloc-2k struct qdisc_rate_table.
qdisc_rtab_list is a single global (not per-netns), so the corrupted
object is shared system-wide.

  BUG: KASAN: slab-use-after-free in qdisc_put_rtab+0x12f/0x160
   qdisc_put_rtab+0x12f/0x160
   tcf_police_init+0xda9/0x1590
   tcf_action_init_1+0x460/0x6b0
   tcf_action_init+0x439/0xa40
   tcf_exts_validate_ex+0x42d/0x550
   fl_change+0xddd/0x7da0
   tc_new_tfilter+0xaa7/0x2420
   rtnetlink_rcv_msg+0x95e/0xe90
  which belongs to the cache kmalloc-2k of size 2048

Protect qdisc_rtab_list and the refcount with a dedicated spinlock. The
(sleeping, GFP_KERNEL) allocation in qdisc_get_rtab() is performed before
taking the lock; if a concurrent inserter added an identical table in the
meantime the freshly allocated one is freed under the lock, so no
duplicate is leaked. qdisc_put_rtab() now decrements the refcount and
unlinks under the same lock.

Link: https://t.co/jVpyyM1R4p

items.content:
RT @ValsAI: New cybersecurity benchmark: SRE-Bench🧵

Models are starting to become competent at finding and patching security vulnerabilities in source code, but can they reverse engineer a binary and understand its behavior?

Many existing cybersecurity benchmarks test model capabilities given a source codebase. But most of the software that actually matters for security- the systems defenders protect and the malware they inspect- only exists as binaries.

This is true on both sides of the threat landscape. Proprietary enterprise software, security appliances, and firmware are frequent attack targets, yet are almost always shipped as binaries. Malware, meanwhile, is deliberately obfuscated to resist inspection. As agents get more capable, binary reverse engineering becomes a critical, under-tested skill.

We worked with collaborators at @Columbia, @ucla, @ucberkeley and @tufts to test this, and we're excited to share SRE Bench: a realistic, contamination-free software reverse engineering benchmark for AI agents. It measures whether an agent can RE a binary well enough to actually understand the underlying code's behavior.

Initial results show real separation between frontier models, and how far there is to go:

RT @yousukezan: LinuxカーネルのPOSIX CPUタイマー処理に、ローカルユーザーがroot権限を取得できるUse-After-Free脆弱性CVE-2026-64560が見つかった。研究者はPixel 10 Proでrootシェル取得を確認し、PoCコードも公開している。

問題は、POSIXプロセスCPUタイマーの削除と、非リーダースレッドによるexec()が競合することで発生する。カーネルがまだタイマーキューに接続された構造体を解放し、その後の処理が解放済みメモリへアクセスする。研究者によると、悪用成功率は50％を超えたという。

Pixel 10 ProではLinux 6.6.118、7月5日リリースのビルドで再現され、取得したroot権限からSELinuxも無効化できたとしている。公開された研究リポジトリには技術詳細とPoCが含まれる。

脆弱性は上流Linuxカーネルで修正済みで、修正前のカーネルが影響を受ける。現時点で実際の攻撃で悪用された事実は確認されていない。記事では、最新のLinuxカーネルおよびAndroidセキュリティ更新の適用を求めている。

items.content:
RT @atomiczsec: ‼️new tradecraft release: I am publishing Blacklight with @SpecterOps, an open-source toolkit and blog for mapping and analyzing the local attack surface created by AI agents on endpoints

local agents are becoming apart of everyday workflows and they leave behind a growing set of endpoint artifacts: session history, configuration, auth material, rules, and other evidence that can matter during an assessment

Blacklight started with one question: what can we learn about AI agent usage from the endpoint itself?

it grew into a two-stage toolkit for safely scouting those artifacts, selectively collecting what matters, and reconstructing agent activity for deeper security analysis

would teams for people to try it, break it, and send feedback
